item.title: Fears spread over Gen Z riot plans across NL
item.description:
Fears spread over Gen Z riot plans across NL

October 30, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

There are fears that a “Gen Z” protest, inspired by the ongoing unrest that has swept through France and other countries, could hit the Netherlands over the weekend.

A report in AD found that groups on Telegram, Snapchat and other social media platforms are preparing to riot in cities including The Hague, Maastricht and Eindhoven.

While no applications for protest permits have been submitted, police have said they generally monitor online forums for signs of trouble but would not comment on this matter specifically.

The messages, which include calls to loot shopping centres, were enough to prompt school heads to issue warnings to parents in Maastricht. Limburg police backed the warnings, according to local broadcaster L1 News.

Shopkeepers in The Hague have also started boarding up their windows as a precaution, as some messaging groups are calling for gatherings on the Malieveld and attacks on commercial centres nearby, according to Omroep West.

The protests in France, which have spread to Italy and Spain began over education and living standards among young people. Many of the demonstrations quickly descended into serious rioting, often with heavy police response.

There are similar concerns in Germany, where youth groups are preparing to protest over similar issues on Halloween.

item.title: “No movement” in cabinet talks amid left-right stalemate
item.description:
“No movement” in cabinet talks amid left-right stalemate

October 30, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The cabinet’s attempt to win over left- and right-wing opposition parties in its ongoing tax plan talks failed again on Friday.

Prime minister Rob Jetten and other senior ministers met opposition leaders a day after three right-wing parties, the far-right JA21, orthodox Protestant SGP and farmer-citizen movement BBB, banded together to push their demands as a single bloc. The demands range from harsher asylum measures and changes to abortion rules to scrapping a tax rise to pay for defence.

The move was the latest attempt by the opposition to force the cabinet to pick a side. Opposition parties have said for weeks that the cabinet will never get a broad agreement, because the two sides of the aisle have incompatible demands.

The offer presented on Friday covered how to pay for changes to box 3, the tax on savings and investments, without raising taxes on wealth, sources told the Telegraaf.

The cabinet would use money left over from a fund to refund people who were overtaxed under box 3 in past years, and cut taxes for business owners who pay themselves profits from their own companies. It would also keep a tax deduction for healthcare costs that was due to be scrapped in 2028.

Regardless of the offer, the stalemate appears to continue. Centre-left PRO leader Jesse Klaver said he saw “no movement at all” on his party’s demand for higher taxes on the wealthy and lower taxes on workers.

JA21 leader Joost Eerdmans called it “a tough, complicated conversation”, but said the new right-wing alliance remained intact.

The coalition of D66, VVD and CDA does not have a majority, so it needs support from opposition parties to get its tax plan through parliament.

item.title: Government seeks to ban smoking where children congregate
item.description:
Government seeks to ban smoking where children congregate

October 30, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The Dutch cabinet wants to prohibit smoking at locations dominated by children, including petting zoos and after-school and other managed playgrounds.

Sources told broadcaster NOS the proposed ban will be discussed at Friday’s Council of Ministers.

While most such places are already smoke-free, the government wants to ensure that the remaining few ban smoking. The House of Representatives also supports the ban and wanted to extend it to other kid-friendly locations like zoos and amusement parks.

That may come in the future, along with bans at unattended playgrounds and outdoor swimming pools, but for now, the government will focus on managed playgrounds and day care centres where there is wide support for the plan.

The ban is part of the government’s efforts to have a smoke-free generation by 2040. Measures already in place include a display ban, unattractive packaging and fewer locations to purchase cigarettes.

item.title: Herman Brood painting added to national art collection
item.description:
Herman Brood painting added to national art collection

October 30, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

A painting by rock legend and artist Herman Brood has been added to the National Collection, placing Brood in the company of Dutch icons such as Rembrandt, Ferdinand Bol, Piet Mondriaan and Karel Appel.

“We believe that Herman Brood should be given more prestige as an icon of the twentieth century as an artist,” said the cultural heritage anency (RCE).

The untitled acrylic work, made with an ever-present injection syringe and paint rollers, features two men with a pistol. It has been hanging on the wall of the tax office in The Hague but was moved earlier this week to the RCE’s depot in Amersfoort, where it’s been given the name “rock-‘n-roll on canvas”.

The inclusion of the work in the 120,000-strong national collection is official recognition that Brood has contributed substantially to Dutch culture and history. The work will be preserved permenantly and can be lent to museums.

“Junkie who painted”

Rob Dupré, a friend of “The Never Be Clever” and “Saturday Night” singer who died in 2001, told broadcaster NOS that Brood would rise from the dead if he heard the news.

“In life, he was seen as a rock ‘n’ roll singer who worked as an artist. Others called him a junkie who painted. As if everyone could do what he did. This news is like winning gold at the Olympics,” said Dupré, who works to detect counterfeits attributed to the artist.

It’s thought the painting ended up in the tax office to pay off a debt. “He didn’t do receipts and that kind of civil matter,” Dupré said. “He painted five paintings and then spent them on alcohol, drugs and women. He wasn’t really businesslike.”

As to the painting now part of the Rijks collection, Dupré says: “Have you ever had an envelope from the Tax and Customs Administration?… He deliberately painted those two people’s sweaters in exactly the same colour.”

As for the gun? “Everyone would want to have that in their hand when you get a tax assessment, right?” Dupré told AD.

Great honour

“He would have thought this was a great honour,” Brood’s wife Xandra Brood told the AD, adding that she had to point out colours to him because the artist was colour-blind. “He worked very fast and made several paintings one after the other.”

She hopes the painting will eventually hang on the walls of Amsterdam’s Stedelijk Museum, his greatest wish.

This painting’s estimated value is 13,000 to 15,000 euros, but Dupré says that’s maybe gone up 50% since the painting became part of the national collection Thursday.

That inclusion, says Dupré, is official recognition of the artist’s craftsmanship. “He was much more than a side-working rock star. And that is now being recognised.”

item.title: French customs seize thousands of THC sweets bound for NL
item.description:
French customs seize thousands of THC sweets bound for NL

October 30, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

French customs officers have intercepted 3,560 packs of cannabis-laced sweets that were being shipped from the US to the Netherlands, the European anti-fraud office OLAF said on Thursday.

The sweets contained THC, the main psychoactive substance in cannabis. Of the packs, 3,213 copied the look of a “very well-known European gummy brand”, using altered lettering to resemble its name. OLAF did not name the brand. All the packs have been destroyed.

OLAF did not say who the sweets were meant to be delivered to in the Netherlands.
In a statement, the agency said the familiar packaging gives the false impression of an ordinary, safe product, but that a single product could contain a high amount of THC, and children could be at risk.

Cannabis sweets have caused several scares in the Netherlands. This summer, Utrecht police warned parents after two children became ill from sweets found in a school playground, broadcaster NOS reported.

item.title: Seven Rotterdam police officers to face trial over arrest death
item.description:
Seven Rotterdam police officers to face trial over arrest death

October 30, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Seven police officers will go on trial in January next year over the death of a 32-year-old man who was held in a “prone position” on the ground for a long time after being tasered during an arrest in Rotterdam in 2023, the public prosecution department (OM) said on Thursday.

Two officers chased the man on June 9 that year, first in a police van and then on foot, after reports that he had crashed his bicycle into a car and then cycled on.

When he ignored their instructions, one officer used a taser, but it did not incapacitate him or stop him from further resisting. More officers arrived and several of them pinned him down. Soon after he became unwell and was given CPR but died in hospital.

In February 2024 the OM said it would prosecute eight officers after an investigation by the Rijksrecherche, which investigates the police. A pathologist concluded the man’s death could have been caused by the way he was restrained.

The officers are accused of breaching the rules on the use of force with fatal consequences, which has been a criminal offence in its own right since July 2022.

The OM said on Thursday it had dropped a case against an eighth officer, as he was still in training and was following instructions.

The case will be heard on January 19 and from February 15 to 18 by the Blauwe Kamer, a special court in Utrecht that handles cases against police officers. The court will rule on all seven cases at the same time.

In September another Rotterdam man, Alfredo Goeloe (51), died during an arrest after collapsing while officers held him on the ground. That incident led to protests in the city. The Rijksrecherche is investigating his death as well.

item.title: You can pry Halloween from my cold, witchy fingers
item.description:
You can pry Halloween from my cold, witchy fingers

October 30, 2026 Molly Quell

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

You can pry the pumpkins from the cold, dead hands of our regular columnist Molly Quell, who is going to celebrate Halloween despite some Dutch naysayers.

I am throwing a Halloween party. I like Halloween. It has cooler vibes than other second tier holidays (Valentine’s Day, Easter) and less stress than the major ones (Christmas, and for Americans/Canadians, Thanksgiving.)

I have gotten some pushback, however, from some of the Dutchies in my life, who are balking at the “Americanisation” of it all.

“What about Sint Maarten?” a Dutch friend asked me, half joking. The traditional Dutch holiday is celebrated on November 11, named after a Roman soldier who converted to Christianity. Children carry paper lanterns and go house to house, singing, in exchange for sweets.

“You are welcome to celebrate it,” I said. “I don’t.”

“I don’t celebrate Halloween,” she retorted.

“I’ll put you down as a ‘no’ then,” I said.

If my friend does celebrate Sint Maarten, she’s in the minority even in the Netherlands. By some estimates, only 30% of kids are out slinging their lanterns (or in some places, hollowed out turnips) for sweet rewards.

In Utrecht the holiday is celebrated widely, as Sint Maarten is the city’s patron saint. Further afield, however, there’s barely a single flame out on a chilly November evening.

Halloween, on the other hand, is everywhere. Hema has pumpkin candles and Takkie in a witch’s hat. There’s trick-or-treating for kids in community centres, spooky canal tours in Amsterdam, horror movies at every Pathé across the country.

That’s significantly better than a hollowed out turnip.

I admit, the broader point my friend was making is correct. American culture is becoming increasingly dominant and, as many become disillusioned with the United States under the current administration, there will be more and more backlash to things seen as symbols of the country.

There are a lot of American things the Netherlands shouldn’t import. I am on record  saying we should ban American influencers from moving here. I am also opposed to importing prudish attitudes towards sex.

Takkie in his little witch’s hat is adorable and I am choosing to defend his (and my) right to celebrate Halloween.

I’ve always been a little surprised that Dutch people don’t embrace Halloween more. They love to dress up in absurd costumes for every other holiday. Have you seen Brabant during Carnival?

Plus, there aren’t really any holidays in autumn. In fact, earlier this year I argued that rather than making Liberation Day (May) a public holiday, as prime minister Rob Jetten suggested, we do Prinsjesdag (September) instead.

Half the country shuts down anyway for the annual announcement of the budget (in 2026, this was even more true, as the train lines were sabotaged) and there’s even a bit of a costume element with the hats.

We need something to celebrate in the fall to take our minds off the impending darkness of winter and Halloween is already right there. It already has built-in rituals, themed food (I will die on this hill defending candy corn) and no obligation to spend time with family.

While the pumpkin spice lattes and the knife-wielding maniacs on film may be an American export, Halloween doesn’t originate in the United States. Historians think it started as a Celtic pagan festival and was taken across the pond by Irish and Scottish immigrants.

And what is a bigger rebuff to the current American administration than celebrating immigration?

item.title: Asylum applications drop 13% under EU migration pact
item.description:
Asylum applications drop 13% under EU migration pact

October 30, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The number of first-time asylum applications in the Netherlands fell by 13% in the third quarter of 2026, compared with the same period last year, according to figures from national statistics bureau CBS and immigration service IND.

The downward trend follows the implementation of the new European Union Migration Pact, which came into effect in June this year, with tighter guidelines, the abolition of permanent asylum residence permits and stricter criteria for family reunification.

Several of those changes echo measures pushed by former asylum minister Marjolein Faber (PVV), who promised the “strictest asylum policy ever” and wanted to make the Netherlands “as unattractive as possible to asylum seekers”. Her emergency asylum law was rejected by the Senate in April.

In the third quarter of 2026, some 5,900 people filed an asylum application for the first time, 850 fewer than a year earlier. Asylum applications from Eritreans and Syrians halved, while 1,500 fewer family reunification applicants came to the country than a year ago.

Eritreans submitted the most asylum claims, followed closely by Syrians. According to CBS, the number of Ukrainian applications increased from 15 to 140, while the number of applications from people from Ethiopia decreased from 290 to 75.

item.title: MPs call for ban on generative AI in primary schools
item.description:
MPs call for ban on generative AI in primary schools

October 30, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

MPs are calling for a ban on AI tools in Dutch primary schools, saying they threaten children’s ability to develop basic reading, writing and critical thinking skills.

A motion put forward by pan-European progressive party Volt and centrist Christian Democrat CDA asks the cabinet to arrange a formal rule disallowing tools like ChatGPT for primary school pupils. So far the motion has the backing of 10 parties with 88 of parliament’s 150 seats, according to broadcaster NOS.

Volt leader Laurens Dassen said in a statement: “I believe in the opportunities AI offers us, but at the same time generative AI is widening learning gaps.”

New learning goals for primary schools, due to take effect in 2027, will require pupils to explore AI and learn to “interact responsibly with an AI system”. In secondary school, students will start experimenting with training AI systems.

The motion tabled by Volt and CDA acknowledges these plans, and doesn’t rule out teaching children about AI, even if they wouldn’t be allowed to use it themselves.

Barend Last, an education specialist who teaches the final year of primary school, told NOS he agreed children should not have unlimited access to AI. However, he also said it can be a useful teaching tool if used in the right way, and that ruling it out altogether risks children learning too little about it.

The PO-Raad, the umbrella body for primary schools, said early research shows pupils learn less when they use generative AI heavily, and that it understood MPs’ concerns. But it said a total ban would come “out of the blue”, and that it would rather reach agreement with the education ministry.

item.title: Cabinet gathers to weigh right-wing bloc’s new joint demands
item.description:
Cabinet gathers to weigh right-wing bloc’s new joint demands

October 29, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Top members of the Dutch cabinet have gathered to discuss demands made on Thursday by a newly formed alliance of right-wing parties that could determine the future of the government’s tax plan.

On Thursday morning, leaders of the far-right JA21, orthodox Protestant party SGP, and farmer-citizen movement BBB announced they are banding together to force concessions in the tax plan negotiations.

They set out their demands – mainly concerning asylum, nitrogen and abortion – in a letter to the cabinet on Wednesday evening.

If their demands are met, the group says, it will support the cabinet on the rest of the tax plan and take a “constructive” approach to the budget.

The parties want to scrap plans to raise taxes to fund defence spending for NATO, as well as a planned VAT rise on flowers, and they want profit exemptions for small businesses raised.

Adjustments to the nitrogen plans demanded by BBB, harsher measures against asylum by JA21, and a pause on late-term abortions, home abortions and surrogacy demanded by the SGP are now joint demands by all three parties.

The move makes prime minister Jetten’s plans for broad support in which parties across the political spectrum back his plans, even more unlikely.

So far, opposition parties on the left and the right have said the coalition must choose a direction: side with left-wing parties like PRO and Volt, or with the right wing. Within the coalition, D66 and CDA prefer the former option, but the VVD has been leaning rightwards.

The letter contains a number of potentially intractable policies. Ending an obligation to the so-called “spreading law”, which requires all councils to house a fair share of asylum seekers, is something asylum minister Bart van den Brink (CDA) has said he cannot commit to.

Dropping the defence tax is particularly sensitive for the CDA. The SGP’s demands on abortion and surrogacy will clash with D66’s stances, broadcaster NOS reported.

The nitrogen proposals also conflict with agreements the cabinet has said are needed to get permits issued again, and PRO has said it will withdraw its support if the nitrogen plans are substantially changed.
